long_biography.plain_text:
After studying at École Polytechnique, Perdriel worked in engineering and water treatment before designing and patenting a compact system that allowed toilets to be installed without conventional large-bore drainage. He built SFA around that invention, expanding sanitary macerators and pumps from French production into international markets. The industrial business, rather than publishing, generated the fortune that supported his wider ambitions.

Perdriel channelled that capital into independent journalism, helping create Le Nouvel Observateur and later founding Le Matin de Paris while developing Challenges and other magazine titles. He involved himself closely in editorial direction even as the publications repeatedly consumed capital. The eventual sale of his remaining magazine interests narrowed his portfolio but left a distinctive record: an engineer-entrepreneur who used manufacturing profits to finance a lifetime in French media.
